Article 23
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector for support in the implementation of protection for women and children in the regional area.
(2) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Kotabaru.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of Regional Government Administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Kotabaru.
- 5 -
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Kotabaru Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit within the scope of the Kotabaru Regency Government.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is an adult human of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
9. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
10. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
11. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, lack of self-confidence or severe psychological suffering in a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
- 6 -
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
18. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Institution is an agency/service/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
23. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services in the context of empowerment of Women and Children victims of acts of violence.
24. Regional Action Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RAD is the basis and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in the context of implementing prevention and protection activities for women and children victims of acts of violence.
25. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
- 7 -
26. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
27. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a direct line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
29. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the annual financial plan of the Regional Government which is discussed and approved jointly by the Regional Government and DPRD and stipulated by Regional Regulation.

Article 8
The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letter c and letter d are that they legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and to protect women and children as family members.

Article 7
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 5 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
(2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.
(3) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

CHAPTER XIII
SANCTION PROVISIONS
Article 29
(1) Every person who intentionally does not provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of acts of violence, allows acts of violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the Laws and Regulations.
(2) If the appointed official or P3A Official for implementing protection does not carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the provisions of the Laws and Regulations.
(3) P3A Officials who carry out service and protection duties for Children and Women from acts of violence and violate service principles may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the internal organizational mechanism.

CHAPTER III
SCOPE
Article 3
(1) The protection of women and children in the region includes prevention, services, and empowerment for victims of physical violence, psychological violence, sexual violence, exploitation, trafficking in persons, and domestic household neglect, including child deviant behavior.
(2) The implementation of protection for women and children from acts of violence is a joint obligation and responsibility among the Regional Government, the community, the family, and parents.
(3) In the region, P2TP2A may be formed, which is the result of a joint initiative between the Regional Government and non-governmental parties.

Part Two
Prevention of Acts of Violence, Exploitation and Neglect of Women and Children

Article 16
The Regional Government through the regional P2TP2A, implements prevention efforts and services for victims of violence, exploitation and neglect of Children and Women up to the empowerment of victims to be able to return to living their lives in accordance with the dignity and worth they possess.
- 13 -

CHAPTER XIV
SPECIAL PROVISIONS
Article 30
(1) The handling of legal cases in the investigation process by law enforcement officials must be handled by special investigators who have been appointed according to their competence by law enforcement institutions for the field of protection of women and children.
(2) Special investigators as referred to in paragraph (1) are:
a. in investigation cases for women or girl children victims of violence must be handled by female investigators;
b. the implementation process as referred to in point a must be in a closed room attended only by the victim's parents or guardian along with the advocacy and psychology team from P3A who have the same gender;
c. in investigation cases for boy children victims of violence may be conducted by male or female investigators, preferably of the same gender and implemented as referred to in point b; and
d. The trial process is not open to the public.

Article 3
Paragraph (1) What is meant by "physical violence" is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death. What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. What is meant by "exploitation" includes:
a. acts that exploit a child economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.
What is meant by "trafficking in persons" is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
What is meant by "Domestic Neglect" is:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as appropriate;
c. acts that neglect a person within the scope of one's household, whereas according to the law applicable to him or her or because of an agreement or contract he or she is obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person;
d. acts that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
What is meant by deviant behavior of children such as the use of Aibon glue which can cause children to feel addicted or intoxicated because they are invited by their friends, and deviation towards free sex behavior or the use of illicit goods.
Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear.

CHAPTER X
REGIONAL ACTION PLAN
Article 25
(1) In order to implement obligations and responsibilities, the regional government establishes action programs and activities for the protection of women and children in 1 (one) RAD as the basis for implementing protection of women and children from acts of violence.
(2) The RAD as referred to in paragraph (1), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).
(3) Further provisions regarding the RAD as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IX
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 26
(1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence.
(2) The Regent may appoint the Head of SKPD whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the protection of women and children to conduct guidance and supervision.

CHAPTER V
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 5
Obligations and responsibilities in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. regional government;
b. community;
c. family; and
d. parents.

Article 2
Paragraph (1)
Letter a Respect for the rights of Children and Women constitutes respect for the fulfillment of basic rights for women and children.
Letter b What is meant by "gender justice and equality" is a condition where every person, both men and women, are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to gain access, as well as welfare; Gender equality is the equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.
Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.
Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of victims" is all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, therefore the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.
Letter e What is meant by restoration of socio-economic rights is increasing understanding, awareness, responsibility, commitment, participation, capability and independence for the purpose of economic improvement and quality of women or target groups so as to avoid problems.

NUMBER 08 YEAR 2014
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
The role of women is very important because they are the mothers of the nation who become the pillars of the family to build the future of human resources in various fields including family economic empowerment, likewise with children who are the generation of the nation who will play a role in filling development in the future.
Children and Women must receive protection from violent treatment, exploitation, human trafficking and neglect by responsible parties. Protection is intended to create a peaceful and prosperous atmosphere for all levels of society in fostering life and togetherness within the regional territory.
Violence cannot be avoided just like that, but must be prevented as early as possible from spreading to a level that is detrimental to all parties. Protection efforts are prioritized on prevention efforts and minimizing incidents.
Acts of violence against Children and Women constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Children and Women victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. Regional Regulations regulate protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Children and Women victims of violence in Kotabaru Regency. As one of the efforts to protect Children and Women, it is carried out through guidance, training and assistance to victims and families of violence victims. Economic empowerment is also carried out for the prevention of women as victims, which can be done by cultivating and developing micro and small enterprises in accordance with local potential. To cultivate micro and small enterprises, it is necessary to increase the capacity and capability of women through assistance and guidance so that women are motivated to start and develop their businesses.

4.4.rationale: The original Indonesian text explicitly includes prevention via education/awareness. Pasal 17(1) lists prevention forms including: (a) “kegiatan sosialisasi peraturan perundang-undangan terkait dengan perlindungan Anak dan Perempuan kepada masyarakat luas” and (g) “penyuluhan/sosialisasi dalam bentuk penyadaran masyarakat luas … khususnya para orang tua”. This is clearly an education/awareness-based prevention strategy. The retrieved English candidates included Article 17 with these exact points, and the judge’s rationale matches the Indonesian meaning. Therefore the golden label “No” appears incorrect.

Considering : a. that women and children with their dignity have the right to be protected from various acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination that marginalize and degrade their dignity as human beings; b. that negative behavior and culture as well as actions that may result in women and children being in a position of pressure or powerlessness in the scope of social community, or in the scope of legal processes should be given special treatment that maintains the stability of their soul and spirit to remain able to carry out their lives in social interaction; c. that the Regional Government is obliged to provide protection for women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children; In View of : 1. Article 5
Sufficiently clear

7.3.rationale: In the Indonesian policy, Pasal 22(2)(e) allows “kerjasama” with “lembaga internasional yang diakui keberadaannya” (recognized international institutions), but this is about cooperation/partnership modalities, not explicitly about international donors or funding. Funding sources are addressed in Pasal 14 (APBD) and Pasal 15(1) (assistance/contributions from individuals, entities, or legally recognized official institutions), without specifying international donors. The judge overgeneralized from ‘international institutions’ cooperation to ‘international donors’/funding involvement, so the predicted “Yes” is not supported for a donors/funding-source indicator. The golden label “No” is consistent with the Indonesian text.
